_comment: ViMove evidence-based program knowledge base. Exercises are limited to movements the in-browser AI can reliably detect (hand open/close, arm raise, leg abduction, mouth, eye blink, sit-to-stand). Rep targets are evidence-informed STARTING points to be individualized with a clinician — not a prescription. Gender is collected for records only; current evidence does not support different exercise SELECTION by gender for these conditions, so it does not change the program.

age_scaling.comment: Targets are individualized: older / more deconditioned users start with fewer reps and progress gradually (ACSM individualized-progression principle).

parkinson.name: Parkinson's disease
parkinson.summary: A movement disorder where exercise is a core, evidence-based part of management — improving mobility, balance and quality of life.
parkinson.summary_tr: Egzersizin, tedavinin temel ve kanıta dayalı bir parçası olduğu bir hareket bozukluğu — hareketliliği, dengeyi ve yaşam kalitesini artırır.
parkinson.principles: Large-amplitude movements (LSVT BIG approach) to counter bradykinesia/hypokinesia, plus strength, balance and facial mobility (for hypomimia).

sources.label: Parkinson's Foundation & ACSM — Parkinson's Disease Exercise Recommendations
LSVT-BIG amplitude therapy — proprioceptive recalibration (BMC Neurology, 2020)

exercises.name: Hand Open - Close
exercises.rationale: Large-amplitude finger extension and full fist closure counter bradykinesia (slowness) and help maintain fine-motor control.

exercises.name: Arm Raise
exercises.rationale: Big-amplitude shoulder flexion follows the LSVT BIG principle of moving bigger to recalibrate undersized movements.

exercises.name: Mouth Open - Close
exercises.rationale: Orofacial movement targets hypomimia (reduced facial expression) and engages the speech/swallowing musculature.

exercises.name: Eye Blink
exercises.rationale: Deliberate blinking activates the orbicularis oculi and addresses the reduced spontaneous blink rate common in Parkinson's.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.rationale: Large-amplitude hip abduction trains lower-limb control and lateral stability for balance.

exercises.name: Sit Down, Stand Up
exercises.rationale: Sit-to-stand builds lower-limb extensor strength and transfer ability (ACSM strength dose ~10-15 reps).

stroke.name: Post-stroke rehabilitation
stroke.summary: After a stroke, high-repetition, task-specific practice drives motor recovery through neuroplasticity. Doing both sides supports symmetry.
stroke.summary_tr: İnmeden sonra, yüksek tekrarlı ve göreve özgü pratik, nöroplastisite yoluyla motor iyileşmeyi sağlar. İki tarafı da çalışmak simetriyi destekler.
stroke.principles: Repetitive, task-specific training (high repetitions) for the upper limb (grasp/release, reach), lower-limb sit-to-stand and hip control, and facial neuromuscular re-education for facial weakness.

sources.label: AHA/ASA — Adult Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery Guideline
Upper-limb motor recovery — UK & European rehabilitation guidelines overview (2023)
Sit-to-stand training with visual feedback in stroke — RCT (2021)
Facial neuromuscular re-education — systematic review (Clinical Rehabilitation, 2022)

exercises.name: Hand Open - Close
exercises.rationale: Repetitive grasp-and-release is core task-specific upper-limb practice; high repetition counts drive motor recovery. Train both sides for symmetry.

exercises.name: Arm Raise
exercises.rationale: Shoulder flexion / reaching is a functional task-specific movement; repeated practice improves upper-limb control.

exercises.name: Sit Down, Stand Up
exercises.rationale: Strong evidence: sit-to-stand training improves lower-limb strength, balance and gait, and trains symmetric weight-bearing.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.rationale: Hip-abductor strengthening supports trunk/pelvis control in the frontal plane, important for balance during standing and gait.

exercises.name: Mouth Open - Close
exercises.rationale: Mirror-guided, slow mouth movements are part of facial neuromuscular re-education for post-stroke facial weakness.

exercises.name: Eye Blink
exercises.rationale: Gentle eye-closure retraining helps restore blink and facial symmetry; keep movements slow and unforced.

arthritis.name: Osteoarthritis & joint mobility
arthritis.summary: For osteoarthritis, gentle exercise is core treatment — it eases stiffness, maintains range of motion, and strengthens the muscles that protect the joints.
arthritis.summary_tr: Osteoartritte nazik egzersiz temel tedavidir — tutukluğu azaltır, hareket açıklığını korur ve eklemleri koruyan kasları güçlendirir.
arthritis.principles: Range-of-motion / flexibility plus low-load strengthening of affected joints, kept within a comfortable, pain-free range (OARSI / ACR core recommendations).

sources.label: 2019 ACR / Arthritis Foundation OA guideline (hand, hip, knee)
OA guidelines across six societies — comparison

exercises.name: Hand Open - Close
exercises.rationale: Range-of-motion finger movement is first-line exercise for hand osteoarthritis — it eases stiffness and preserves grip and dexterity.

exercises.name: Arm Raise
exercises.rationale: Gentle shoulder range-of-motion keeps the joint mobile and reduces stiffness; move only as far as is comfortable.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.rationale: Hip abduction maintains hip range of motion and strengthens the abductors that support the hip and knee joints.

exercises.name: Sit Down, Stand Up
exercises.rationale: Sit-to-stand strengthens the quadriceps — a core recommendation for knee osteoarthritis — kept gentle and within a pain-free range.

balance.name: Balance & fall prevention
balance.summary: Building leg strength is a proven way to reduce falls in older adults. This program follows the strengthening core of the Otago Exercise Programme.
balance.summary_tr: Bacak gücünü artırmak, yaşlılarda düşmeleri azaltmanın kanıtlanmış bir yoludur. Bu program, Otago Egzersiz Programı'nın güçlendirme çekirdeğini izler.
balance.principles: Lower-limb strengthening (quadriceps via sit-to-stand, hip abductors) plus controlled reaching — the strength component of Otago, which lowers falls by ~35%. Standing-balance holds should be added under professional supervision.

sources.label: Otago Exercise Programme — manual (ACC New Zealand)
Otago programme for fall prevention — systematic review
WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity & Sedentary Behaviour (falls)

exercises.name: Sit Down, Stand Up
exercises.rationale: Sit-to-stand builds quadriceps strength — a key Otago component shown to lower fall risk and ease everyday transfers.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.rationale: Standing hip abduction strengthens the hip abductors that stabilize the pelvis during standing and walking.

exercises.name: Arm Raise
exercises.rationale: Controlled reaching trains the shoulder and posture muscles used to recover balance and stay upright.

general.name: General senior fitness
general.summary: A balanced, full-body maintenance routine in line with WHO physical-activity guidance for adults aged 65+ — to keep strength, mobility and independence.
general.summary_tr: 65 yaş üstü için DSÖ fiziksel aktivite kılavuzuna uygun, dengeli ve tüm vücudu çalıştıran bir bakım rutini — güç, hareketlilik ve bağımsızlığı korumak için.
general.principles: Multicomponent activity: muscle strengthening of all major groups plus functional movement, as recommended by the WHO for older adults to maintain function and prevent falls.

sources.label: WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour (at a glance)

exercises.name: Arm Raise
exercises.rationale: Shoulder strengthening maintains upper-body function for everyday tasks like reaching and carrying.

exercises.name: Hand Open - Close
exercises.rationale: Opening and closing the hands maintains grip and fine-motor control for daily independence.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.rationale: Hip abduction strengthens the lower-limb and pelvis-stabilizing muscles used in walking.

exercises.name: Sit Down, Stand Up
exercises.rationale: Sit-to-stand maintains the leg strength needed for everyday transfers and helps prevent falls (WHO multicomponent recommendation).
